description: Declarative pass/fail expectations the explore-grader checks the explorer's output against. Purely natural-language assertions -- no code -- same shape as the production pattern this repo is inspired by.

cases.name: login
cases.description: Sauce Demo login page -- the simplest possible case, good smoke test for the whole pipeline.

expectations.text: A username input field is identified with a semantic primary locator (placeholder or label), not CSS/XPath
A password input field is identified with a semantic primary locator
A login submit button is identified by role=button and accessible name/text
None of the three core elements (username, password, login button) have count > 1 for their primary strategy
The accessibility tree was captured and referenced as the basis for at least one element's accessibility_node

cases.name: inventory
cases.description: Product listing page reached after login -- tests whether the explorer can navigate through an auth step and enumerate a repeated component (product cards).

expectations.text: At least one 'Add to cart' button is identified with role=button and a semantic locator
The explorer notes that multiple 'Add to cart' buttons exist (one per product) and flags this repetition rather than treating it as a single ambiguous locator error
A sort/filter control for the product list is identified
The shopping cart icon/link in the header is identified with a semantic locator
context.md explains how per-product buttons are distinguished from each other (e.g. by nearby product name) if flagged as a testability gap

cases.name: cart
cases.description: Cart page reached after adding an item -- tests precondition-state navigation (login -> add to cart -> view cart) in one crawl.

expectations.text: A 'Checkout' button is identified with a semantic primary locator
A 'Remove' button for the cart item is identified with a semantic primary locator
The element map correctly reflects that this page required prior navigation state (not directly reachable from a fresh session) if the explorer attempted a cold visit
